You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

from collections import defaultdict

def transform(grid):
    h,w=len(grid),len(grid[0])
    cells=[(i,j,grid[i][j]) for i in range(h) for j in range(w) if grid[i][j]]
    for name,key in [("anti",lambda i,j:i+j),("row",lambda i,j:i),("diag",lambda i,j:i-j)]:
        m=defaultdict(set)
        for i,j,v in cells: m[key(i,j)].add(v)
        if not all(len(s)==1 for s in m.values()): continue
        line={k:next(iter(s)) for k,s in m.items()}
        p=len(line); assign={}; bad=False
        for s,v in line.items():
            r=s%p
            if r in assign and assign[r]!=v: bad=True; break
            assign[r]=v
        if bad or len(assign)!=p: continue
        f=lambda i,j: assign[key(i,j)%p]
        return [[f(i,j) for j in range(w)] for i in range(h)]
    raise ValueError

```python
def transform(grid):
    h,w=len(grid),len(grid[0])
    cells=[(i,j,grid[i][j]) for i in range(h) for j in range(w) if grid[i][j]]
    for name,key in [("anti",lambda i,j:i+j),("row",lambda i,j:i),("diag",lambda i,j:i-j)]:
        m=defaultdict(set)
        for i,j,v in cells: m[key(i,j)].add(v)
        if not all(len(s)==1 for s in m.values()): continue  # Skip if any group has multiple values
        line={k:next(iter(s)) for k,s in m.items()}
        p=len(line); assign={}
        bad=False
        for s,v in line.items():  # For each (key, value)
            r = s % p
            if r in assign and assign[r] != v:  # Check for conflicts
                bad=True; break
            assign[r] = v
        if bad or len(assign) != p: continue  # Skip if there's a conflict or incomplete
        f=lambda i,j: assign[key(i,j)%p]
        return [[f(i,j) for j in range(w)] for i in range(h)]  # Return filled grid
    raise ValueError  # If none of the transforms work
```

The code tries anti-diagonal first, then row, then diagonal. For each:
1. Group cells by the key function (anti= i+j, row= i, diag= i-j)
2. Each group must have a SINGLE value, otherwise skip
3. For each group, assign the value to position (key % period)
4. Check that there are no conflicts (two different values mapping to same position)
5. If no conflicts and all positions covered, return the filled grid
